hypothesis: Replace terminal-epoch publication with likelihood-constrained corpus-support checkpoint selection: retain each of the same five corpus-only language-model epochs, admit checkpoints whose held-out token NLL is within 0.03 of the best epoch, and publish the admitted checkpoint with the highest fixed seeded distinct corpus-novel valid ancestral-sample rate. This makes usable de novo support, rather than epoch number alone, decide which otherwise unchanged autoregressive prior and frozen representation enter every objective.
method_thesis: Pretrain a task-agnostic autoregressive SMILES model and its sequence representation only on the allowed unlabeled corpus, retain a frozen prior, and restart all task-local state for each independent objective. Fit a probabilistic surrogate only to the ten fixed scored molecules and subsequent oracle-evaluated molecules, while maintaining an oracle-anchor policy updated only from returned true scores. Before each evaluator-announced batch, clone that anchor into a disposable inner policy, optimize the clone without oracle calls using the surrogate posterior mean as its molecular reward, and ancestrally sample a fresh ephemeral set of complete SMILES from the resulting policy. Canonicalize locally, remove invalid, previously evaluated, and duplicate molecules, and select the requested number by greedy batch expected improvement; after feedback, refit the surrogate, update the oracle anchor from the real observations, and discard the inner clone. Thus every submitted molecule is generated de novo, the corpus is never scored or searched as a candidate pool, and surrogate feedback changes the source distribution itself before acquisition rather than merely ranking proposals from a fixed generator. The optimization target is solely the equal-weight mean of the five independent terminal Top-1 scores.

activation_observables.measurement: For each preparation seed, define the rate as the number of distinct complete canonical molecules absent from the union of the selected training and held-out corpus identities divided by all ancestral verification draws. On a verification stream disjoint from the checkpoint-selection stream, sample both the actually published likelihood-constrained checkpoint and that same training trajectory's terminal epoch with paired derived seeds and identical temperature, length limits, and draw count. Report each rate, published-minus-terminal paired difference, the three-seed mean paired difference and improved-seed count, while retaining every failure and collision category in the denominator. Also report every epoch's held-out NLL and selection-audit rate and verify that the published checkpoint is the exact argmax among checkpoints within 0.03 NLL of the best. The Parent reference is terminal publication, with observed corpus-novel counts 411/512, 399/512, and 403/512 across its three preparations.

applicability_conditions: At least one nonterminal checkpoint must retain held-out token likelihood within 0.03 NLL of the best epoch while offering genuinely higher corpus-novel valid support; otherwise terminal publication is already optimal under the registered rule and no checkpoint replacement occurs.

The fixed seeded selection audit must be representative enough that its support ordering transfers to the disjoint verification stream; tiny apparent differences caused only by finite ancestral-sampling noise are not expected to transfer.

Downstream search must benefit from additional valid, unique corpus-novel mass in the shared prior without requiring the absolute lowest held-out next-token NLL. The mechanism is weaker when reward-relevant chemistry is outside all five checkpoints' support or when surrogate geometry, rather than generator support, is the dominant limitation.

All checkpoint decisions use only the allowed unlabeled corpus and the protocol-supplied preparation seed. No task identity, oracle score, objective-specific molecule, or later run-mode state is available during selection.

The selected state must remain compatible with the Parent's unchanged vocabulary, dimensions, BOS/EOS/padding semantics, autoregressive likelihood and sampling calls, and fixed-width normalized embedding consumer; this experiment does not claim transfer if checkpoint replacement requires any downstream interface change.
research_intent.falsifier: The mechanism did not produce the claimed behavior if the published state is not the registered support-rate argmax inside the NLL tolerance, if its held-out token NLL exceeds the best epoch by more than 0.03, if the published state hash equals the terminal checkpoint on all three preparations because no earlier eligible checkpoint wins, or if the mean published-minus-terminal distinct corpus-novel valid rate on the disjoint verification audits is non-positive. If the rate increases with a valid checkpoint replacement but terminal score does not, the mechanism activated but the hypothesized score transfer was not useful.
research_intent.implementation_change: Keep the Parent's corpus reservoir, split, vocabulary, GRU architecture, next-token objective, optimizer, five epochs, state-dictionary/configuration artifact interface, sequence-embedding function, sampling interface, and every run-mode Layer unchanged. During preparation only, retain a CPU copy of the model state after each epoch, compute held-out token NLL, and run an equal-size deterministic selection audit using a generator derived solely from the protocol-supplied preparation seed. After all five epochs, restrict eligibility to checkpoints no more than 0.03 token NLL above the minimum observed held-out NLL, select the eligible checkpoint with the greatest distinct complete canonical molecule rate absent from both selected training and held-out corpus identities, and break exact ties by lower NLL and then later epoch. Load and publish only that selected state. For activation evidence, use a separate derived-seed verification audit to sample the selected and terminal checkpoints under identical bounded settings; log both rates, their paired difference, selected epoch, all per-epoch NLL and selection rates, state hashes, and exhaustive non-completion, parse, connectedness, size, canonicalization, corpus-collision, and duplicate counts. Selection and verification samples remain diagnostics only and never become scored candidates or a persistent candidate library.

research_intent.observed_bottleneck: Parent n-c555e44c6daf always publishes the terminal fifth language-model epoch, even though checkpoint choice uses neither ancestral support nor novelty. Across its three independently prepared artifacts, held-out token NLL reduction is strong (mean 3.710592644414861), but 303 of 1,536 fixed audit draws are parse failures and only 1,213 of 1,536 draws are novel to the selected corpus; unique-valid support varies from 0.78515625 to 0.814453125. All downstream sessions still fill their batches, so this is not an execution failure, but the Parent leaves a measurable corpus-prior support bottleneck while assuming that the lowest terminal token loss is also the best de novo checkpoint. Its macro score also varies across seeds (0.513626533890974 to 0.575798548411393), with especially large per-task deviation on deco_hop and sitagliptin_mpo, although the existing evidence does not establish that preparation support causes that score spread.

applicability_conditions: For these three corpus preparations, terminal epoch 5 is already the exact support-rate argmax among all five checkpoints, including every checkpoint within 0.03 NLL of the best. The evidence therefore does not support checkpoint replacement on the observed trajectories.

The implementation is operational when an eligible nonterminal checkpoint exists: all seeds retained multiple eligible epochs, the selection rule was exactly reconstructible, the separate selection and verification streams ran, and the selected artifact remained loadable by every unchanged downstream consumer. Benefit additionally requires a nonterminal eligible checkpoint to beat the terminal support audit, which was not observed.

Transfer of selection-stream ordering to a disjoint verification stream remains untested because selected and terminal were the same state on all three seeds. A future applicability claim requires at least one actual nonterminal winner and a positive pooled paired verification difference, preferably with a margin robust to 512-draw sampling noise.

The corpus-only boundary and frozen interfaces are supported: selection occurs only during preparation from the protocol seed and unlabeled corpus diagnostics, the two-file vocabulary/model configuration remains compatible, and all 15 downstream sessions complete. This establishes compatibility, not a support-rate or score benefit.

No evidence here supports the hypothesis that additional prior corpus-novel mass improves downstream search, because the intervention supplied no additional mass. That transfer question is only applicable after a genuine checkpoint replacement changes the published state.

possible_failure_causes: The necessary checkpoint-replacement opportunity did not occur. Although nonterminal checkpoints were NLL-eligible on every seed, terminal epoch 5 had the largest selection-stream corpus-novel valid rate within every eligible set: 404/512 versus 402/512 and 383/512 on seed 0, 406/512 versus 395/512 on seed 1, and 394/512 versus 377/512 and 337/512 on seed 2.

No earlier checkpoint had a higher selection support rate even outside the NLL-eligible set on any observed seed, so merely widening the 0.03 tolerance would not have produced a replacement for these trajectories.

The 512-draw selection audit is finite and the seed-0 eligible terminal advantage over epoch 4 is only 2/512. Sampling noise can therefore affect close orderings, but here it cannot establish activation: the registered rule still selects the terminal state, and the paired verification comparison is necessarily identical.

Because the published state equals the Parent terminal state on every seed, downstream task behavior and scores are unchanged by construction. This result does not diagnose a failure in the inherited surrogate, anchor, generator, or acquisition Layers; it isolates the absence of a checkpoint-selection intervention.

The disjoint verification stream has lower aggregate support than the separate stream-37 Parent diagnostic, 1,193/1,536 versus 1,213/1,536, illustrating audit-stream variation. That cross-stream difference is not a checkpoint effect; the valid paired comparison uses stream 43 on both selected and terminal states and is exactly zero.

activation_observables.measurement: For each preparation seed, define the rate as the number of distinct complete canonical molecules absent from the union of the selected training and held-out corpus identities divided by all ancestral verification draws. On a verification stream disjoint from the checkpoint-selection stream, sample both the actually published likelihood-constrained checkpoint and that same training trajectory's terminal epoch with paired derived seeds and identical temperature, length limits, and draw count. Report each rate, published-minus-terminal paired difference, the three-seed mean paired difference and improved-seed count, while retaining every failure and collision category in the denominator. Also report every epoch's held-out NLL and selection-audit rate and verify that the published checkpoint is the exact argmax among checkpoints within 0.03 NLL of the best. The Parent reference is terminal publication, with observed corpus-novel counts 411/512, 399/512, and 403/512 across its three preparations.
activation_observables.name: prior_corpus_novel_valid_rate

applicability_conditions: At least one nonterminal checkpoint must retain held-out token likelihood within 0.03 NLL of the best epoch while offering genuinely higher corpus-novel valid support; otherwise terminal publication is already optimal under the registered rule and no checkpoint replacement occurs.

The fixed seeded selection audit must be representative enough that its support ordering transfers to the disjoint verification stream; tiny apparent differences caused only by finite ancestral-sampling noise are not expected to transfer.

Downstream search must benefit from additional valid, unique corpus-novel mass in the shared prior without requiring the absolute lowest held-out next-token NLL. The mechanism is weaker when reward-relevant chemistry is outside all five checkpoints' support or when surrogate geometry, rather than generator support, is the dominant limitation.

All checkpoint decisions use only the allowed unlabeled corpus and the protocol-supplied preparation seed. No task identity, oracle score, objective-specific molecule, or later run-mode state is available during selection.

The selected state must remain compatible with the Parent's unchanged vocabulary, dimensions, BOS/EOS/padding semantics, autoregressive likelihood and sampling calls, and fixed-width normalized embedding consumer; this experiment does not claim transfer if checkpoint replacement requires any downstream interface change.
research_intent.falsifier: The mechanism did not produce the claimed behavior if the published state is not the registered support-rate argmax inside the NLL tolerance, if its held-out token NLL exceeds the best epoch by more than 0.03, if the published state hash equals the terminal checkpoint on all three preparations because no earlier eligible checkpoint wins, or if the mean published-minus-terminal distinct corpus-novel valid rate on the disjoint verification audits is non-positive. If the rate increases with a valid checkpoint replacement but terminal score does not, the mechanism activated but the hypothesized score transfer was not useful.
research_intent.implementation_change: Keep the Parent's corpus reservoir, split, vocabulary, GRU architecture, next-token objective, optimizer, five epochs, state-dictionary/configuration artifact interface, sequence-embedding function, sampling interface, and every run-mode Layer unchanged. During preparation only, retain a CPU copy of the model state after each epoch, compute held-out token NLL, and run an equal-size deterministic selection audit using a generator derived solely from the protocol-supplied preparation seed. After all five epochs, restrict eligibility to checkpoints no more than 0.03 token NLL above the minimum observed held-out NLL, select the eligible checkpoint with the greatest distinct complete canonical molecule rate absent from both selected training and held-out corpus identities, and break exact ties by lower NLL and then later epoch. Load and publish only that selected state. For activation evidence, use a separate derived-seed verification audit to sample the selected and terminal checkpoints under identical bounded settings; log both rates, their paired difference, selected epoch, all per-epoch NLL and selection rates, state hashes, and exhaustive non-completion, parse, connectedness, size, canonicalization, corpus-collision, and duplicate counts. Selection and verification samples remain diagnostics only and never become scored candidates or a persistent candidate library.
research_intent.mechanism: Replace terminal-epoch publication with likelihood-constrained corpus-support checkpoint selection: retain each of the same five corpus-only language-model epochs, admit checkpoints whose held-out token NLL is within 0.03 of the best epoch, and publish the admitted checkpoint with the highest fixed seeded distinct corpus-novel valid ancestral-sample rate. This makes usable de novo support, rather than epoch number alone, decide which otherwise unchanged autoregressive prior and frozen representation enter every objective.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: Parent n-c555e44c6daf always publishes the terminal fifth language-model epoch, even though checkpoint choice uses neither ancestral support nor novelty. Across its three independently prepared artifacts, held-out token NLL reduction is strong (mean 3.710592644414861), but 303 of 1,536 fixed audit draws are parse failures and only 1,213 of 1,536 draws are novel to the selected corpus; unique-valid support varies from 0.78515625 to 0.814453125. All downstream sessions still fill their batches, so this is not an execution failure, but the Parent leaves a measurable corpus-prior support bottleneck while assuming that the lowest terminal token loss is also the best de novo checkpoint. Its macro score also varies across seeds (0.513626533890974 to 0.575798548411393), with especially large per-task deviation on deco_hop and sitagliptin_mpo, although the existing evidence does not establish that preparation support causes that score spread.
